pdf.bannerInvalid: At least one signature is invalid — the document may have been altered.
pdf.bannerUnknown: At least one signature could not be verified: the signer's identity is not trusted.
pdf.bannerValid: Signed and the signature is valid.
pdf.bannerValidMany: Signed and all {n} signatures are valid.
pdf.chkIntact: The document has not been modified since this signature was applied.
pdf.chkModified: The content was CHANGED after signing (a later revision modifies the document).
pdf.chkRevocation: No revocation data (CRL/OCSP) is embedded in the file; online revocation checking is not done.
pdf.chkTampered: The signed content was altered or the signature is corrupted.
pdf.chkUpdatedSafe: Later revisions only add signatures / validation data — the signed content is unchanged.
pdf.defaultHint: Windows does not let apps make themselves the default: after registering, choose DevStation and tick "Always use this app" in the Windows dialog.
pdf.defaultIs: DevStation is the default app for PDF files.
pdf.defaultNot: DevStation is not registered to open PDF files.
pdf.defaultRegisteredNot: Registered, but another app is still the default for PDF files.
pdf.docGone: The file content is no longer in memory — reopen the file.
pdf.dropHint: Tip: drag & drop PDF files here. Ctrl+O to open, Ctrl+F to search.
pdf.homeHint: View PDF files and check their digital signatures — no Acrobat needed.
pdf.idChainIncomplete: The signature is intact, but the signer's identity can't be confirmed: the certificate of the issuing CA "{ca}" is not embedded in the file and could not be downloaded, so the chain can't be built. You can trust the signer's certificate directly, or install that CA in Windows.
pdf.idError: Could not validate the signer's certificate: {err}
pdf.idExpired: The signer's certificate (or a CA in the chain) had expired at signing time.
pdf.idNotYetValid: The signer's certificate was not yet valid at signing time.
pdf.idUntrustedRoot: The signature is intact, but the signer's identity can't be confirmed: the certificate chain ends at "{ca}", which this computer does not trust (it is not in the Windows certificate store and has not been trusted in DevStation). If you trust this CA, click Trust below.
pdf.noSignatures: This document has no digital signatures.
pdf.sigValidModified: Signature is valid, but the document was changed after signing
pdf.timeNow: the document has no signing time, so the current time was used
pdf.timePdf: from the time written in the PDF (signer's clock, not protected)
pdf.timeSigner: from the signer's clock (included in the signature)
pdf.timeTsUnverified: from a timestamp that could not be fully verified
pdf.trustManagerHint: Certificates you trusted in DevStation (stored only on this computer, separate from the Windows certificate store). Certificates already trusted by Windows do not need to be added.
pdf.trustRootHint: Do this only if you know this CA (e.g. Vietnam National Root CA, your company's CA).
pdf.unregisterConfirm: Remove DevStation from the apps that can open PDF files?
pdf.defaultDone: DevStation is now the default app for PDF files.
pdf.defaultNotChosen: The default PDF app was not changed — pick DevStation and tick "Always use this app" in the Windows dialog.
pdf.defaultDev: This is a dev build: the registration points to the debug exe and only works while npm run app:dev is running. Set the default from the installed app.
pdf.sigRevoked: Signature is INVALID — the certificate was revoked
pdf.sigDocmdpViolated: Certification is INVALID — the document was changed in a way it does not allow
pdf.chkRevoked: The certificate "{cert}" was REVOKED on {time} (embedded {src}) — before the signing time.
pdf.chkRevokedAfter: The certificate "{cert}" was revoked on {time} (embedded {src}), after the verified signing time.
pdf.chkNotRevoked: The certificates are not revoked (checked with the {src} embedded in the file).
pdf.chkWeakHash: The signature uses the weak hash algorithm {alg}; it is intact but not considered fully valid.
pdf.chkDocmdpViolated: Certification signature ({p}) — the document was changed after certification in a way that is NOT allowed.
pdf.docmdp2: only form filling and signing allowed
pdf.docmdp3: form filling, signing and comments allowed
pdf.bannerRevoked: At least one signer's certificate was revoked before signing — that signature is invalid.
pdf.bannerDocmdp: The document was certified but then changed in a way the certification does not allow.
pdf.bannerModified: The signatures are intact, but the document content was changed after signing.
pdf.bannerWeak: At least one signature uses a weak algorithm (SHA-1).
pdf.idIssuerMismatch: The certificate chain is broken: "{cert}" says it was issued by "{issuer}", but the CA found for it is named "{ca}" (same key, different name — typically a certificate from a TEST/staging CA). Under X.509 rules the names must match, so trusting the root does not help. Only trust this signer's certificate directly if you know it.
pdf.noteFallback: The signing software records the algorithm as "rsaEncryption" (1.2.840.113549.1.1.1) — valid and common (Viettel, FPT, VNPT…), but not supported by the main verification library. DevStation verified it with its own checker: the signature, the content digest and the timestamp are correct ({alg}).
